Told of in: A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills (GE 1,489); The Hollow Man seen again (GE 2,457); The covered hearth spreads (GE 2,460).

23.note: Pilgrims sit a night at the line of the trees without entering; their small fires lie all along the edge. Told of in: Pilgrims at Coille Naomh Muileann chiar (GE 2,449).

24.note: A child of Cnoc bheag went past the line of stones and was not found; the settlers take timber only from the far side of the river. Told of in: A child lost in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag (GE 2,451); The first house at Cnoc bheag (GE 2,453).

28.note: The obelisk with the unread line and the four Dia-thìris words. Told of in: Carragh Cnoc bheag raised (VE 4,672); The older face of Carragh Cnoc bheag (VE 4,718).

29.note: Cuimhnich an teine, in its ring of fire-cracked stones. Told of in: Colbh Cnoc chiar raised (VE 4,770); A ring of fire-stones round the pillar (VE 4,812).

30.note: After Anndra Breac was put out of the ford for saying "we came", the saying on the column is spoken as a rule at the opening of the gathering; its worn words are recut by a hand from the hill (GE 4,364). Told of in: Anndra Breac says 'we came' (GE 2,422); The doctrine said at the column (GE 2,423); The saying on the column recut (GE 4,364).

31.note: Ruin of Seann-Dhaoine' outpost; the households of Cathair mhòr below take no stone from it. Told of in: Làrach an Dùin-fhaire abandoned (VE 4,023); Cathair mhòr below the old outpost (GE 2,847).

32.note: Ruin of Làrach an Dùin; the fishers of Ceann mhin will not go up to it. Told of in: Làrach an Dùin abandoned (VE 4,124); Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore (GE 3,028).

33.note: Làrach an Teampaill: the Dia-thìrich pass it without stopping, and a path is worn round it at a distance. Told of in: Làrach an Teampaill abandoned (VE 4,275); The temple ruin avoided (GE 3,357).

34.note: A cairn for each head of a household at death, on the slope above the cattle-fold; some forty by the end of the age. Told of in: Muileann chaol on its hill (GE 3,218); Cairns on the hill at Muileann chaol (GE 3,264).

37.note: The gathering at the eight wind-stones of Ceann leathan ends with wrestling and the lifting of stones; the black boulder lies there still. Told of in: The wind-stones of Ceann leathan (GE 2,084); Ceann leathan's contests (GE 3,403).

38.note: Raghnall Ceannfhionn and the holder of An Cnoc Ruadh agreed salt for wool here; it became the yearly gathering. At An Cruinneachadh Mòr (GE 3,000) the holders set their hands in the king's with four hundred of his blood about him. Both king-lists were recited here whole. Told of in: Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace (GE 1,175); The ford gathering (GE 1,208); Lines recited at the ford (GE 2,247); The great gathering at the ford (GE 3,000); The ford gathering grows (GE 3,450); The two lists recited together (GE 4,347).

39.note: A boat hollowed from one oak trunk, long enough for six, sunk and left at the landing. Told of in: The dug-out at Cidhe Beag (GE 716).

40.note: The panthers turn back at the foothills (a hard winter follows); cattle driven into the passes out of season are taken. Told of in: The panthers turn back (GE 2,428); The cattle lost in the passes (GE 2,428); The panther season kept at Baile dhomhain (GE 2,447).

41.note: A family by the burial ground takes on the clearing of thorn; diggers break into a grave lined in Seann-Dhaoine' manner, close it and move the row. Told of in: The Tuam keepers (GE 2,447); A grave at Tuam opened (GE 2,447).

46.note: The keeper's cup and its three copies set side by side on a flat stone and filled from the spring in turn. Told of in: The meeting of the cups (GE 2,408).

48.note: Binnean a' Chlachair. Told of in: The snowflake coal takes fire in the air (VE 2,170).

add.name: the crowning in the grove
add.note: Ailean kept the seven fires seven nights, fasting; on the eighth Caoran came with the Tuath Dè and named him Rìgh Chlann nan Dè, and put into him the power that was in the coals. Told of in: The vigil and the crowning (GE 1).

add.name: Àth na Fala
add.note: The ford where Sluagh an Ear comes against the king. The battle opens the next day: he holds it alone three days and three nights, the dead of the host dam the river, and he falls on the third night. The ford is called Àth na Fala after. Told of in: Ailean Mòr falls at Àth na Fala (FE 1); Dùn dhearg will not bow (GE 4,520); The eve of the Binding (GE 4,550).

add.name: the boundary stones of Dòmhnall Clachach
add.note: Marker stones along the valley below the hill, parting the grazing of Dùn ìseal from its neighbours'; some still stand and are argued over. Told of in: Dòmhnall Clachach sets the boundary stones (GE 107).

add.name: where An Cnoc Ruadh knelt
add.note: Uisdean Mòr came down to the lake shore and knelt to the king. Told of in: The Red Hill bends the knee (GE 290).

add.name: the shingle of Baile ghorm
add.note: Iain Dubh, the king's son, was slain here raiding the salt; the king came down alone, and none struck. Tràigh an t-Salainn became his without blood. Told of in: Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid (GE 672); Iain Dubh killed (GE 727); The king at Baile ghorm (GE 728).

add.name: the keepers' house and the stone cup
add.note: A house for the holder of the lot, its door facing the slab; Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill's cup of grey stone, the measure of every handful; the coal of Gilleasbuig Beag laid back under the slab. Told of in: The keepers' house (GE 2,404); The stone cup (GE 2,405); The coal returned to the crack (GE 2,411).

add.name: the hawk lintel of Àth mhòr
add.note: A hawk carved over a house door, wings closed, head turned: the oldest carving of any bird on the island. Told of in: The hawk lintel at Àth mhòr (GE 1,853).

add.name: the wolf graves of Tobar fhiadhaich
add.note: Wolves buried whole and with care, laid on their sides as people are. Told of in: Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich (GE 1,890).

add.name: Gilleasbuig Beag's island
add.note: The keeper who took coal was rowed out to Eilean chrom and left without a boat; his fire was seen three nights. The island stays empty and unfished. Told of in: Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal (GE 2,409); Gilleasbuig Beag's island (GE 4,373).

add.name: the tide-rock of Ros dhomhain
add.note: High-water marks cut at an even interval on a boulder in the harbour mouth; Seònaid Mhòr cut hers in pairs. A third rock is kept at Inis thais. Told of in: A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain (GE 1,708); The lake is higher (GE 1,747); The keepers of the Ros dhomhain rock (GE 2,424); A third tide-rock at Inis thais (GE 2,424).

add.name: the stone of A' Ghaoth Dhubh
add.note: A stone set in the midst of Ceann chiar with a mark for every house A' Ghaoth Dhubh took: twenty-two. Told of in: A' Ghaoth Dhubh (GE 2,417); The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar (GE 3,726).

add.name: the white stones of the fault
add.note: A line of white stones along the crack; no house within a stone's throw. Broken in two places when the ground shook again, and laid again. Told of in: The fault-line kept clear (GE 847); The ground shakes at Cill ghlas again (GE 3,863).

add.name: the first trench for another vein
add.note: Diggers from Dùn ìseal opened it seeking coal like the vein's and left it when two were crushed. A second opening elsewhere found common rock, and the prospecting ended. Told of in: The first seeking of another vein (GE 2,267); The stone that would not break (GE 2,289); The prospecting ends (GE 2,312).

add.name: the tally wall of Seann Warr
add.note: Seann-Dhaoine' counting stones built into a wall, some three thousand strokes; they thicken together in the bad years. Told of in: The tally wall of Seann Warr (GE 389); The bad years in the counts (GE 470).

add.name: Clach nan Dà Stràc
add.note: The last tally stone of Seann-Dhaoine, two strokes finished and a third begun and forsaken. Told of in: The half-cut stone of Seann Chwen (GE 510); The Seann-Dhaoine fall silent (GE 551).

add.name: the wind-stones and the eight notches
add.note: Eight tall stones on the point at Ceann leathan. Told of in: The naming of the wind directions (GE 2,047); The wind-stones of Ceann leathan (GE 2,084); The wind-names carried to the islands (GE 2,124).

add.name: Eilean ìseal, the island of the dead
add.note: The households of the south-east coast begin to row their dead here after the old manner of Seann-Dhaoine. Told of in: Eilean ìseal given to the dead (GE 4,370).

add.name: the long-house of Cathair gheal
add.note: Forty paces long, byre and hall under one roof; twice burned and twice rebuilt on the same footing. Told of in: The long-house at Cathair gheal (GE 1,416).

add.name: the wind-stone of Seann Chwen
add.note: A wind-name cut in the Dia-thìreach manner over an older mark of Seann-Dhaoine. Told of in: The wind-stone at Seann Chwen (GE 2,447).

410.note: The fishers of the south-east coast keep to Seann-Dhaoine' lane. Told of in: The ancient sea-way (VE 4,375).

add.name: Rathad na Spor
add.note: Worn by the flint-carriers from Cnoc àrsaidh south and east toward Cruinneachadh an Àtha; near Àth leathan their feet sink it a yard deep. Told of in: The flint of Cnoc àrsaidh (GE 1,781); The flint road (GE 1,817).

add.name: Rathad an t-Salainn
add.note: From the pans of Baile ghorm by Cruinneachadh an Àtha to the north-west; at Muileann àrsaidh salt costs three times its price at the pans. Told of in: The salt road to the north-west (GE 2,468); Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill (GE 1,247).

add.name: the stepping-stones of the Abhainn fhionn
add.note: The first made crossing of any river on the island. Told of in: The river crossings of Abhainn fhionn (GE 3,628).

add.name: the road of the salt and wool (An Cnoc Ruadh to the ford)
add.note: Murchadh Gearr walked Rathad an t-Salainn every year to be seen on it; Dùn chrom's bank faces both ways between An Cnoc Ruadh and the hills of the vein. Told of in: Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill (GE 1,247); Dùn chrom raised (GE 2,801).

1.note: Pots left full of boiled bark and seaweed; the grave-rows doubled. The oldest hunger tied to a place. Told of in: The hunger at Baile chrom (GE 1,966).

2.note: The springs run dry so long that the field banks are forsaken; the fields are cut anew on another line. Told of in: The drought at Achadh shean (GE 2,006); Achadh shean resettled (GE 3,125).

3.note: A crack a man could fall into; a spring moves a hundred paces downhill and back. Told of in: The ground opens at Cill ghlas (GE 827); The ground shakes at Cill ghlas again (GE 3,863).

4.note: Sand a hand thick with deep-water shells over the hearths; the second wave takes no house. Told of in: The wave at Cnoc chaol (GE 777); A second wave on the south coast (GE 3,817).

add.name: the first kingdom: the hill and its valleys (GE 1)
add.note: Ailean takes the hill and brings the households of the valleys under his hand. Told of in: Ailean Mòr, first of the Stone Kings (GE 1).

add.name: An Cnoc Ruadh bends the knee (GE 290)
add.note: An Cnoc Ruadh keeps its holders and swears to the king. Told of in: The Red Hill bends the knee (GE 290).

add.name: Tràigh an t-Salainn bends the knee (GE 728)
add.note: No blood is shed and none is paid. Told of in: The king at Baile ghorm (GE 728).

add.name: the great gathering at the ford (GE 3,000): the north and the west set their hands in the king's
add.note: Only the households east of the vein send no one. Told of in: The great gathering at the ford (GE 3,000).

add.name: A' Ghaoth Dhubh
add.note: Strips the thatch from every house of the east coast from Cuan ruadh to Ceann chiar; the coast feeds Cuan ruadh through the winter from its shared surplus. Told of in: A' Ghaoth Dhubh (GE 2,417); The sharing holds after the Black Wind (GE 2,417).

add.name: Sluagh an Ear
add.note: The households east of the vein, sworn to owe nothing to Dùn ìseal, gather their spears at Dùn dhearg. Told of in: Dùn dhearg will not bow (GE 4,520); The eve of the Binding (GE 4,550).

add.name: the last counts of Seann-Dhaoine (GE 308–551)
add.note: Strokes on midden stones, Balla nan Stràc of Seann Warr, the count at Seann Tarr; the bad years on three coasts at once; Clach nan Dà Stràc; silence. Told of in: Strokes on the midden stones (GE 308); The tally wall of Seann Warr (GE 389); The count at Seann Tarr (GE 428); The bad years in the counts (GE 470); The half-cut stone of Seann Chwen (GE 510); The Seann-Dhaoine fall silent (GE 551).

add.name: the moor takes the north (GE 3,588)
add.note: The oak falls back; heather, birch and bog-moss spread over the northern lowlands and the winters lengthen. Told of in: The moor takes the north (GE 3,588).
Rìoghachd Chlann nan Dè. Told of in: Ailean Mòr, first of the Stone Kings (GE 1).

add.text: Cha do thàinig sinn; bha sinn ann
add.note: We did not come; we were here. Told of in: The doctrine said at the column (GE 2,423).
